title: Barcelona’s Joan Garcia expected to miss up to three weeks with calf injury
content:
Barcelona are hopeful of having goalkeeper Joan Garcia back in time for their Champions League quarter-final at the start of April.

The 25-year-old picked up an injury in the 83rd minute of Barcelona’s 7-2 win against Newcastle United in the last 16 decided on Wednesday night. He had to be replaced by back-up Wojciech Szczesny.

Club sources told The Athletic that, after initial tests, Barca believe Garcia has sustained a minor injury to his right calf. It is expected to keep him sidelined for up to three weeks, and further examinations are set to take place on Thursday at Barcelona’s training centre.

Speaking after the game, Barca head coach Hansi Flick said: “It (Garcia’s injury) does not look very serious, but we have to wait for the tests.”

The first leg of Barcelona’s Champions League quarter-final will be played week commencing Monday, April 6 – against either Atletico Madrid or Tottenham Hotspur.

Garcia joined Barcelona in the summer of 2025, after the club activated the the €25million (£21.4m, $28.8m) release clause in his Espanyol contract, and has had an impressive debut campaign. He has established himself as Barcelona’s number one goalkeeper, playing 35 games in all competitions, including seven in the Champions League.

After saving a shot from Newcastle’s Harvey Barnes, Garcia then held his right calf after going to ground. The Spanish goalkeeper was substituted minutes later.

Garcia may have been in contention for a call-up to the Spain national team for their March fixtures – the friendlies against Serbia (March 27) and Egypt (March 30).

Barcelona’s final match before the March international break sees them host Rayo Vallecano in La Liga on Sunday.
